findings.text: Provides read access to the globally configured architected timer frequency for other timer users.
Reports whether event stream is marked available on the calling processor, documented as safe from preemptible context because availability is stable across resume.
Exposes singleton virtualization timer metadata object shared with hypervisor hosting code.

Offers cross timestamp service combining hypervisor time with counter value; reports unsupported when discovery is disabled or hypervisor signals failure, otherwise fills host time and optionally cycle count and counter identity.

Device tree probe entry performing one time initialization; ignores extra nodes, discovers interrupts, configures rate and capabilities, selects interrupt kind, then registers per processor events and counters.

ACPI probe entry performing one time initialization; rejects duplicate bring up, maps non secure interrupts, requires valid hardware frequency, derives always on behavior, then registers events and counters.

Memory mapped frame probe claiming and mapping frame registers, resolving operating frequency with overrides, acquiring frame interrupt, then publishing event device and clocksource; failures before publication abort.
Memory mapped interrupt entry acknowledging only when status shows expiry, masking further signaling before invoking generic event callback; otherwise reports unhandled.
Frequency configuration is sticky with first setup winning and later calls having no effect; device property overrides caller supplied value when present, and invalid result triggers warning.

Counter plumbing chooses virtual or physical read routines from execution mode and selected interrupt kind, substituting stabilized variants when workaround is active; publishes chosen reader for timekeeping and scheduler clock, sizes masks from hardware width, marks suspend behavior, and seeds virtualization time tracking from current count.

Registration acquires per processor event storage, per processor interrupts suited to chosen timer kind including paired secure plus non secure case, power management notification and hotplug hooks; any failure releases earlier acquisitions and returns error.
Common bring up always emits banner before registering counters and delegating to architecture specific event setup.

Interrupt selection prefers hypervisor virtual when in hypervisor mode with valid interrupt and no known breakage, otherwise falls back; outside hypervisor without hypervisor present it prefers virtual when available, otherwise chooses non secure physical on 64-bit and secure physical elsewhere.
Virtualization metadata always records virtual interrupt; physical interrupt is recorded only when kernel runs in hypervisor mode.

Device tree discovery uses named interrupt lookup when interrupt-names is present and indexed lookup otherwise; always-on negates to derive idle stop behavior, arm,no-tick-in-suspend enables suspend stop, and on 32-bit arm,cpu-registers-not-fw-configured forces secure physical choice; missing interrupt for chosen kind aborts.
ACPI path takes frequency strictly from hardware register and fails when validation rejects it; always on capability comes from firmware table query for chosen interrupt.

PTP service selects KVM_PTP_VIRT_COUNTER for virtual interrupt kinds and KVM_PTP_PHYS_COUNTER otherwise, invokes vendor hypervisor PTP function, converts combined high and low result words to host time, optionally combines second pair to cycle, and reports CSID_ARM_ARCH_COUNTER as counter identity.

Memory mapped timer object bundles event member evt with clocksource member cs, shared block pointer gt_block, mapped base base, access selector distinguishing PHYS_ACCESS versus VIRT_ACCESS, and operating frequency rate.
Embedding allows recovering enclosing timer object from pointer to its event member or its clocksource member.

Power management cycle saves control register and clears local event stream mark on entry; on failed entry or exit it restores control and re-sets local mark when stream feature is present, always reporting success.
Power management hookup has two build variants: one registering and unregistering notifier with warning on unregister failure, and one doing nothing and reporting success.
Processor offline path stops local timer by disabling its per processor interrupts, including non secure companion when present, and reports success.

One shot programming requires disabled state before updating compare value; implementation disables when needed, computes target as current count plus requested delta, writes compare then enables with interrupt unmasked. Shutdown only clears enable.

Frame choice maps control base, reads capability identifier, then probes each valid frame by attempting to enable all access permissions and reading back what persists; first virtual capable frame with virtual interrupt wins, otherwise remembers last physical capable frame with physical interrupt; unmaps before returning.
Memory mapped count read selects physical or virtual low word offset by access type and repeats high low high triplet until both high samples agree, combining halves into 64-bit value.

Memory mapped event publication advertises one shot with dynamic interrupt capability under name arch_mem_timer, rating 400, possible processor affinity, span from 15 to 56-bit maximum; clocksource publication uses name arch_mmio_counter, rating 300, continuous flag and 56-bit mask, both keyed to same frequency, with event interrupt enabled after registration and initial state forced to shutdown.
Memory mapped frequency prefers hardware frequency register, overridden by clock-frequency property when node and property are present, falling back to global architected rate when both yield zero.

Frequency based clocksource registration is scale registration with unit multiplier; per processor interrupt request without explicit affinity delegates with empty affinity; managed interrupt request delegates to threaded variant adding conditional oneshot semantics; scheduler clock registration in this configuration performs no action; monotonic to calendar conversion delegates to nanosecond conversion.

Duplicate initialization is either ignored with warning or rejected; absent interrupt for chosen kind aborts; invalid frequency warns or fails depending on firmware path; known broken virtual timer taints as out of specification; suspend stop flag reflects whether counter halts in suspend; compare programming is not atomic and requires disabled timer; frame mapping or reservation failures abort before publication.
No explicit locks appear; coordination uses per processor event objects and per processor saved control plus local test set clear of shared availability mask.
Control identifier offset is 8; virtual capability for frame n is value 2 shifted left by 4 times n.
Frame access control base is 64 with stride 4 per frame index.
Access permission bits are 0 for physical count read, 1 for virtual count read, 2 for frequency read, 3 for offset read, 4 for virtual timer write, 5 for physical timer write.
Within a frame physical count starts at 0, virtual count at 8, frequency at 16, physical compare at 32 with control at 44, virtual compare at 48 with control at 60.
Memory mapped event rating is 400 with minimum delta 15 and maximum derived from 56-bit mask; clocksource rating is 300 with 56-bit mask.
Memory mapped driver log lines carry fixed arch_timer_mmio prefix.
Boot banner reports configured frequency in megahertz with two decimal digits together with human name of selected interrupt.
Broken hypervisor virtual timer detection matches machine against list containing brcm,bcm2712; on match it marks kernel tainted as out of specification and emits single warning.
